docs.title: Syncing with your local Actions project
docs.text:
DEE actions live in the MES database — but your customization project keeps local .cs copies of them (conventionally under Cmf.Custom.Data/DEEs) for IntelliSense, code review, and source control. The Sync commands keep the two sides aligned in bulk: compare, download what changed on the MES, upload what changed locally.

All three commands work against every DEEs folder, subfolders included. The folders are auto-detected in your workspace (one per Data package), or listed in the deeDebugger.deesFolder setting. The commands are available from the … menu in the DEE Explorer's title bar or the Command Palette:

  • Sync: Compare Local DEEs with MES
  • Sync: Download Changes from MES
  • Sync: Upload Local Changes to MES

Start with Compare — it classifies every action. Download and Upload each run the same comparison first and act on its results. Both directions preserve the marker contract: only marker bodies move, wrapper boilerplate never shows as diff noise.

docs.title: Comparing local vs MES
docs.text:
Sync: Compare Local DEEs with MES scans your local DEE files and the server's actions and reports: in sync / differ / local-only / MES-only. From the results you can open a per-file diff editor for anything that differs.

Two things make the diff readable:

  • Only real code differences are highlighted. The server side of the diff is rendered inside your local file's wrapper — so the generated boilerplate never shows as noise; you compare marker bodies against marker bodies. Differences only in line endings, trailing whitespace, or blank lines at the start or end of a body count as in sync.
  • Both marker dialects are understood. Files with the generated /** START/END OF USER-DEFINED … **/ markers and files in the older cmf-cli authoring dialect (//---Start DEE Code--- / //---End DEE Code--- and the condition pair) are both recognized. DeeDevBase.cs is skipped automatically.
  • Subfolders and several packages are scanned. bin, obj and the extension's own .dee-debug/ working copies are not.

MES-only entries open read-only so you can inspect before downloading.

docs.title: Downloading
docs.text:
Sync: Download Changes from MES shows the changed/new entries pre-checked; deselect what you don't want, confirm, and the extension writes the files:

  • Actions you've never had locally are written as complete generated files in the primary DEEs folder (the first one).
  • Actions you already have keep your local file's layout — only the marker bodies are updated.

A summary reports how many files were written and lists any failures.

docs.title: Dirty-editor protection
docs.text: Warning avoided: if a file selected for download (or an action you reload) is open in an editor with unsaved changes, the extension skips it rather than overwrite the disk under your editor. Skipped files are counted as failures and named in the summary. Save or revert the editor, then run the download again for those entries.

docs.title: Uploading
docs.text:
Sync: Upload Local Changes to MES shows the locally changed files; pick the ones to push. Each is compiled and saved on the MES (the same operation as Save Action to MES per file):

  • A compile failure in one file does not abort the batch — the rest upload, and the summary names the failures, with the errors in the Problems panel against the right files.
  • If an action changed on the MES after the comparison, that entry fails, and the output log tells you to run Sync: Compare again — so you never blind-overwrite a colleague's change. Re-compare, review the diff, then re-upload.
  • Files with damaged markers are left out of the comparison, so they are never uploaded; the DEE Debugger output log names each skipped file and why (see the marker contract). If that action exists on the MES, it is listed as MES only. Downloading it does not overwrite the damaged file: the entry fails, and the output log says why. Fix the markers (or move the file), then compare again.
  • Local-only files create new actions on the MES — enabled, with your file's bodies, as version 1 in state Active (not effective). They run already — with no effective version the MES uses the highest — but a version staged later would take over. At the end of the batch the extension lists the created actions and offers Make Effective; choose Keep as Drafts to promote them later from the tree. Either way they now appear in the tree (with a not effective badge while drafts) and compare as in sync.

The upload is cancellable mid-batch from the progress notification.

docs.title: A typical git workflow
docs.text:
With the Actions project in git, sync gives you reviewable DEE changes:

  1. Baseline: on a clean working tree, run Sync: Download Changes from MES for everything. Commit. Your repo now mirrors the MES.
  2. Develop: edit actions in VS Code — single-action loop (edit / debug) — and save your final versions to the MES.
  3. Capture: run Sync: Compare to confirm repo vs MES state, download anything changed server-side (your own MES-UI edits, a colleague's change), and commit with a meaningful message. git diff shows exactly what changed in each action body.
  4. Apply elsewhere: on a branch checkout or another environment (switch with the Status Bar item), run Sync: Compare then Sync: Upload Local Changes to MES to push the repo's state to that MES.
  5. Review: pull requests over the DEEs folder review actual rule changes; because downloads preserve layout and skip whitespace churn, diffs stay minimal.

Note: Sync transfers action code. Action group membership and evaluation order are managed in the MES UI (Administration → DEE Actions) or via Data package installation — not by this extension. Enabled/effective state is not synced either, but the tree shows it (disabled, not effective badges) and Make Version Effective is one click away.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Find your symptom below. Two habits solve most problems fast:

docs.title: Step 1: open the DEE Debugger output channel
docs.text: View → Output, then select DEE Debugger in the dropdown on the right. Every operation logs there — timestamped, with the environment and version information support needs, and with credentials automatically redacted. Many error notifications also offer to open it. When a fix below says "check the output channel", this is the place.

docs.title: Step 2: prove the basics with Test Connection
docs.text: Run DEE Debugger: Test Connection from the Command Palette. Its result splits the world in two: "Could not reach …" means a connectivity/address problem (Connection problems); an authentication error means a token problem (Expired tokens).

docs.title: Expired tokens (the 1-hour problem)
docs.text:
Symptoms: everything worked, and now every operation fails with an authentication error (HTTP 401/403) and the hint "The token may be expired — run 'DEE Debugger: Set Credentials…' to set a new one.". Refresh fails, uploads fail, debug toggle fails.

Why it happens: on MES stacks that use the Security Portal — which includes the standard local development stack — browser-copied access tokens expire after 1 hour. (Only stacks without the Security Portal issue ~14-day tokens.) One hour into your session, the token dies mid-work. This is the most common problem users report, and it is not a bug in your code or the extension.

Confirming it's the cause:

  • The error mentions 401/403 or "token may be expired".
  • The output channel shows your token's type and expiry time on the failure — look for the [auth] stored credential: … line. A negative "min from now" value means the token has expired, and by how long.
  • Operations that don't touch the MES (editing locally) still work; everything that talks to the server fails.

Fix now: get a fresh token and run DEE Debugger: Set Access Token… (see how to copy one from the browser).

Fix forever: use a Personal Access Token. Generate it in the Security Portal → your user security page → Personal Access Tokens, then in VS Code:

  1. DEE Debugger: Set Personal Access Token… — paste the PAT. (Setting a PAT automatically clears any stored access token for that environment, so it takes effect immediately — you don't need to Clear Credentials first.)
  2. Refresh the tree to confirm.

Other token pitfalls:

Symptom Cause / fix A freshly copied token is rejected immediately It was truncated when copied — these tokens are 1–2 KB. In the browser DevTools, use right-click → Copy value on the Authorization header, and paste without the Bearer prefix. Set a browser access token after a PAT, still hitting auth errors A stored access token always takes precedence over the PAT — even after it has expired. Run Clear Credentials, then set the credential you actually want. Token works in one environment but not another Credentials are stored per environment — set the token while the right environment is active.

docs.title: Connection problems
docs.text: Symptom Likely cause / fix "Could not reach the MES host at …" The stack is down (docker ps should show the MES containers — start it with cmf dev local stack up), or the host address is wrong. Verify from the same shell VS Code uses: curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' <address>/api/ping should print 200 (or 401 — that still proves routing). Same, but a debug session is active The host is probably paused at your breakpoint — a stopped debugger suspends the whole MES. Press Continue (F5) and retry. See everything freezes. Works in a terminal, not in VS Code (or vice versa) — WSL setups Windows and WSL have different networks. Use the address that works for curl in the same environment VS Code runs in (check the bottom-left remote indicator: WSL window vs local window). "returned a login page instead of data" The address answered with an HTML page instead of the API. Usually the token was rejected (revoked or expired) and the forward-auth served the login page — set new credentials. If the token is fine, the address is wrong (wrong port, or a sub-path instead of the base URL the MES UI uses, e.g. http://localhost). "returned unparseable JSON" The address answered with something that is neither JSON nor an HTML page. Point the environment at the base URL the MES UI uses (e.g. http://localhost, not a sub-path). Devcontainer stack unreachable from outside; docker ps shows only the devcontainer (image vsc-…) Your stack runs docker-in-docker. Use the Docker-in-docker (devcontainer) environment type — and re-check the devcontainer's IP and name, which change on restart/rebuild. See the decision tree. Everything broke after a devcontainer rebuild Same as above: new random container name, possibly new IP. Update the environment via Manage Environments…, or pin the name in devcontainer.json.

docs.title: Extension or tree problems
docs.text: Symptom Likely cause / fix The extension doesn't activate / no DEE Debugger icon The Microsoft C# extension (ms-dotnettools.csharp) is missing — it's a required dependency. Check the Extensions view for an install error; on offline machines install it manually. Also: the workspace must be trusted, and a folder must be open. Tree is empty but Test Connection succeeds Check the tree isn't filtered (a filled filter icon in the DEE Explorer title = a text filter is active — click it and clear). Also check the rows at the top of the tree: "N DEEs matched '…'" (filter) and "N disabled actions hidden". A specific action doesn't appear in the tree Draft (not-yet-effective) actions are shown, with a not effective badge. If it is missing it is either disabled (the tree shows a "N disabled actions hidden — click to show" row; click it or enable deeDebugger.showDisabledActions) or excluded by a text filter. See the FAQ. An action never runs A not effective badge is not the cause on its own: with no effective version the MES runs the highest version. Check that the action is enabled and belongs to an action group (MES UI). If you staged a new version, the effective one keeps running until you make the new one effective (right-click → Make Version Effective). Tree shows a different environment's data than expected Check the green Connected · … row at the top of the tree and the MES: status-bar item — you may be on another environment. Click to switch.

docs.title: Uploads and compile errors
docs.text: Symptom Likely cause / fix Upload fails with errors in the Problems panel A real compile error in your code — click the entry to jump to the line, fix, re-upload. The raw server message is in the output channel. Upload refused: "marker problems" A marker line was deleted, duplicated, or edited. Don't fix by hand — copy your body code out, run Reload Action from MES, paste back inside the markers. See the marker contract. Upload refused: changed on the MES since it was loaded Someone else saved the action meanwhile. See concurrency conflicts. Upload fails with an authentication error Token expired — see above. My local file changed on disk by itself Not a bug: with debug mode on, the MES host rewrites the file when its regenerated wrapper differs from yours — typically because something was edited outside the markers (e.g. a hand-added using). Keep all edits inside the markers and use UseReference(...) for extra assemblies.

docs.title: Debugging problems
docs.text: Symptom Likely cause / fix "spawn docker ENOENT" (or "docker: not found") on toggle/attach The docker CLI isn't on the PATH of the environment VS Code runs in. Verify docker ps in VS Code's integrated terminal. On WSL setups, docker must work inside the same remote. Toggle/attach fails with a container error naming the engine or container The environment's container plumbing is wrong — wrong container name (custom_host vs host), stale devcontainer name/IP, dead remote context. The error and output channel name the failing command; fix the environment. "vsdbg was not found … Install it now?" Normal on a fresh container — choose Install vsdbg and the extension installs the debugger. On MES 12 hosts the download runs inside the container (the image has curl), so the container needs internet access. MES 11.x images have no curl/wget, so the extension downloads vsdbg on your machine and streams it in — that needs internet plus bash + tar locally (on Windows, run VS Code in WSL). Either way, a wrong engine/container config also fails here (see previous row). Attach fails with Unknown Error: 0x80131c08 Wrong process picked — choose the dotnet process running Cmf.Foundation.Services.HostService.dll, never the first/wrapper process. If it persists, the container may lack debugging privileges; on Kubernetes the pod spec must allow SYS_PTRACE. Process picker is empty The debugger isn't installed in the container yet, or the engine/container settings point at the wrong place — check the output channel for the probe result. Attach "works" but DEE breakpoints never bind, and no error appears anywhere On a Linux-containerized host that is not patched for DEE debugging (#158143), every debug-mode execution fails to compile inside the host — nothing reaches the extension. Since 0.2.0 the host is probed when you enable debug mode or attach, and you are prompted to patch; if you chose Continue Anyway or turned the probe off (deeDebugger.hostPatchCheck), run Patch Host for DEE Debugging (dev/test)… now, then re-toggle debug mode. Breakpoint never hits (action clearly runs) Almost always one of: (1) the action ran as a different user than your token — debug mode is per-user (FAQ); (2) the action hasn't executed since you enabled debug mode (breakpoints bind on first execution — hollow until then); (3) a load balancer sent the execution to another host instance — point the environment at one instance directly; (4) the host restarted and dropped the registration — accept the re-enable prompt, or toggle debug off/on. Executing a debug-mode action fails: "code is invalid … Unexpected error writing debug information -- 'Value cannot be null. (Parameter 'type')'" The Linux host debug-symbols bug (MES up to 11.x) — a product issue, not your code. The error notification offers Patch Host for Debugging…; accept it (the host restarts), then re-enable debug mode. See the Linux prerequisite. After a stack recreate the extension offers the patch again. Debug worked, then silently stopped after a host/stack restart In-memory registration lost. The extension prompts to re-enable when it notices; if in doubt, toggle debug off and on, re-attach, and (Linux) re-apply the PDB patch after a recreate. MES UI / API / colleagues frozen while you debug You're paused at a breakpoint — the whole host process is suspended. Press Continue (F5). Expected behavior. Breakpoint binds but opens a read-only copy of the file The path mapping between container and your local folder drifted (e.g. the DEEs folder moved, or debug mode was enabled by version 0.2.0 or older). Toggle debug mode off and on to re-register, then re-attach. "Several local files belong to '…'" when opening an action Two DEEs folders (usually two Data packages) both contain <ActionName>.cs. Keep one, or list only one package in deeDebugger.deesFolder. "… exists but has no valid DEE markers — the extension will not overwrite it" A file with the action's name exists but its markers are damaged, or it is not a DEE file. Fix the markers or move the file, then open the action again. "… is outside …, which the debugger maps to …" when enabling debug mode The file is outside the folder the host path maps to. Keep DEE files inside the workspace folder. With useMount, only files inside the mounted DEEs folder can be debugged.

docs.title: When you're stuck: Collect Support Bundle
docs.text:
Before contacting support (or your internal tools team), run:

DEE Debugger: Collect Support Bundle…

The extension gathers everything a support engineer needs to diagnose without a screen-share — versions and platform, the active environment's configuration, token metadata (type, expiry — never the token itself), session and debug state, live connectivity probes, and the recent output-channel log (secrets redacted).

It opens as a document in your editor — nothing is written to your project or sent anywhere automatically. Review it, remove anything you consider sensitive, then save it or paste it into your ticket.

A good ticket = the support bundle + what you did (which command, which action) + what you expected + what happened.

docs.title: Tutorial: your first DEE debug session
docs.text:
From an empty VS Code window to a breakpoint hit inside a running MES — in about 30 minutes. Each part ends with a Checkpoint; don't move on until it holds, and if it doesn't, the linked troubleshooting row will unblock you.

You need before starting:

  • A development MES stack you're allowed to play with (e.g. cmf dev local stack up in your customization project) — never a shared or production instance.
  • The extension VSIX, VS Code 1.145+, and a working docker CLI (details: Getting started — what you need).
  • A MES login that can open Administration → DEE Actions in the MES UI.

docs.title: Part 1 — Install and open a workspace (≈ 5 min)
docs.text:
1. Install the extension: drag the .vsix onto the Extensions view, or code --install-extension dee-debugger-<version>.vsix. The Microsoft C# extension installs alongside it as a dependency.
  2. Open a folder — ideally your customization project (the one with Cmf.Custom.Data/DEEs); any empty folder also works for this tutorial.
  3. If VS Code asks about Workspace Trust, choose Trust.

Checkpoint 1: the DEE Debugger icon is on the Activity Bar, and clicking it shows the "Connect to a development or test MES" welcome view with a Discover Environments button. (Prefer a guided tour? DEE Debugger: Open Getting Started mirrors Parts 1–5 as a VS Code walkthrough.) (No icon? → extension doesn't activate.)

docs.title: Part 2 — Create a scratch action to play with (≈ 5 min)
docs.text:
Never learn on a real business rule. In the MES web UI:

  1. Log in (on a local stack: http://localhost) and go to Administration → DEE Actions.
  2. Create a new action named Tutorial_MyFirstDee — any classification, no action group needed. (Action names may contain only letters, digits and underscores, and must start with a letter — no dots.)
  3. Action code: Input["touched"] = 1; Test condition: return true;
  4. Save it.

Checkpoint 2: Tutorial_MyFirstDee exists in the MES UI's DEE Actions list.

docs.title: Part 3 — Connect (≈ 5 min)
docs.text:
1. In the DEE Explorer's welcome view, click Discover Environments and wait for the probe to finish.
  2. Select your stack (reachable ones are pre-checked) and choose Connect. (Nothing found? Your topology needs a manual profile — detour to the connection decision tree, then come back.)
  3. When prompted for credentials, the extension asks how you'd like to authenticate. Use a Personal Access Token if your Security Portal offers them (user security page → Personal Access Tokens), via Set Personal Access Token…. Otherwise copy an access token from the browser (how) — noting it will expire in 1 hour on Security Portal stacks, which is fine for this tutorial.

Checkpoint 3: the tree shows a Connected · \<environment> row (green plug icon), action groups underneath, and Tutorial_MyFirstDee near the root (it has no group — group names nest as folders, ungrouped actions sit at the root). The Status Bar shows MES: \<environment>. (Tree empty or errors? → Connection problems.)

docs.title: Part 4 — Open, edit, upload (≈ 5 min)
docs.text:
1. Click Tutorial_MyFirstDee in the tree. A file Tutorial_MyFirstDee.cs opens: generated usings, a wrapper class, and your two code snippets between marker comments.
  2. Read this once, it's the golden rule: only edit between the START/END markers — the wrapper is server-owned and edits to it get discarded and can cost you work (the marker contract).
  3. Inside the USER-DEFINED CODE markers, add a line:
Input["greeting"] = "hello from vs code";
  1. Save the file (Ctrl+S). Notice the action's pending upload badge in the tree — the MES is not updated yet.
  2. Hover the action in the tree and click its cloud-upload icon (Save Action to MES (Compile & Save); also in the Command Palette). Expect a brief saved to MES message in the status bar and the pending upload badge to clear.
  3. See what failure looks like, so you recognize it later: add a broken line inside the markers (var oops = ;), save, upload again. The upload fails and the Problems panel points at the broken line. Delete the line, save, upload — clean again.

Checkpoint 4: the MES UI's DEE editor shows your greeting line in Tutorial_MyFirstDee, and the Problems panel is empty. (Upload failed without a compile error? → likely the expired token.)

docs.title: Part 5 — Debug it (≈ 10 min)
docs.text:
Mental model in one sentence: debug mode makes the host compile your file with debug symbols for your user only, hot-reloading on every save — colleagues and the stored version are untouched (full model).

  1. Linux host prerequisite (MES 11 and older containerized stacks): the host must emit cross-platform debug symbols; unpatched hosts fail with a "writing debug information" error due to a known product bug. You don't need to check this yourself: when you enable debug mode the extension probes the host and, if needed, offers Patch Host for Debugging (one click, the host restarts). MES 12 images already contain the fix. Details: the Linux prerequisite.
  2. Right-click Tutorial_MyFirstDee → Enable DEE Debug Mode (or the bug icon on the row). A DEBUG badge appears (the row icon turns into a bug), the status bar shows 🐞 1, and a dialog asks whether to attach the debugger now — its text explains the semantics.
  3. Choose Attach Debugger. The very first attach shows a one-time dialog listing the prerequisites — choose Attach. On a fresh container, accept the offer to install the debugger (vsdbg) — this takes a minute. The extension then attaches to the MES host process (if a picker appears, choose the dotnet process running Cmf.Foundation.Services.HostService.dll).
  4. Set a breakpoint on your Input["greeting"] = … line (click in the gutter). A hollow circle is normal — it binds when the action first executes.
  5. Trigger the action: right-click it in the tree → Execute Action… → keep the input as {} → choose a read-only execution.

The breakpoint hits. The editor jumps to your line; inspect Input in the Variables pane, hover variables, step with F10.

  1. While paused, notice the freeze: the MES UI and API don't respond — a stopped debugger suspends the whole host (why). Press Continue (F5) to let it finish; the execution report opens with your output values. Continue within a minute: the extension gives up on a MES request after 60 seconds, and Execute Action… then reports a failure instead of opening the report.
  2. Feel the hot reload: without any upload, change the greeting text, save (Ctrl+S — the status bar flashes "DEE: pushed"), and run Execute Action… again. The breakpoint hits with the new value — the MES database still holds the old code.

Checkpoint 5: you've hit a breakpoint twice, the second time on code you never uploaded. (Breakpoint never hit? → debugging problems — the top cause is triggering the action as a different user than your token's.)

docs.title: Part 6 — Clean up (≈ 2 min)
docs.text:
1. Right-click the action → Disable DEE Debug Mode to turn debug off — the stored version takes over again (the 🐞 count in the status bar disappears).
  2. Disconnect the debugger (the plug icon on the debug toolbar).
  3. If you want the greeting change kept, it's already on the MES from Part 4's upload flow — otherwise upload your final state, or delete Tutorial_MyFirstDee in the MES UI.
